statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20%, the floor of the watch band, on orderly two-way Nasdaq-100 discovery after a fully retraced session low, while Stress stays high at 74% on a 24-year-peak yield backdrop and a Brent move above $100.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 12:30Z September employment report through the hour after the 13:30Z US cash open on 2 October, the single forecast hour mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a completed retracement as yields retreat from a 24-year peak, while Brent above $100 keeps Stress high
body: Verified evidence at the assessment cutoff shows the Nasdaq-100 at 30,536.25, up 0.42% against a 30,408.50 previous close, inside a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range. The defining structural fact is a completed retracement: the morning low was fully recovered and the index trades in the upper half of the range, 80 points below the session high and 234 below the 52-week high, rather than pinned at an extreme. Implied volatility decayed from a 17.59 high to 16.33, close to the 16.21 session low. The whole Treasury curve richened, with the 2-year at 4.80% (-11bp), the 5-year at 5.02%, the 10-year at 5.24% after peaking at 5.34%, its highest since 2002, and the 30-year at 5.61%; the quarterly rise in 10-year yields was the largest this century. Energy is the one aligned amplifier: Brent gained 4.58% to $102.52 and WTI 3.04% to $93.17 after Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports and PetroChina cancelled cargoes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict, in which Hormuz crude flows have recovered to roughly 13.5 million barrels a day while about 3 million barrels a day of refined products remain absent. Today's US releases were firm: initial jobless claims 197,000 against 200,000 expected and a fourth consecutive weekly decline, continuing claims 1.701 million, ISM Manufacturing 54.5 against 55 expected with new orders at 55.3 and production at 56.7, and construction spending up 0.9%. Sector tone is mixed, with semiconductors supported after Micron's results and the KBW bank index down 0.7% on rate pressure. Because yields are retreating and volatility is decaying, the amplifier set is not aligned, so Tail holds the 20% watch floor while Stress stays high at 74%. The shared Finviz context file was roughly 44 hours old and marked partial, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are available from published Claude assessments. Tail ranged 20-25% and the mapped state was WATCH in 23 of the 24 hours, with a single orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES hour at 06:00Z when Tail touched 25% during a trend-up European phase. Stress climbed from 70% overnight to a 78% peak around 14:00Z as the global bond selloff pushed the 10-year to a 24-year high, then eased to 74-75% as yields retreated. Confidence held 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast window holds the watch band through the US close, the futures halt and the Asian session, with Tail at 20-21% and dominant mode normal to mixed while China's national holiday thins regional flow. Risk then builds into 2 October: Tail reaches 24% for the 12:30Z September employment report and 25% for the 13:30Z cash open, the single orange hour and the narrow danger window, before easing to 21-24% as post-event price discovery is scored. Stress peaks at 79% around the release and returns to 74% by 18:00Z.
